question: During an MSE, you observe: elevated and expansive mood, rapid pressured speech, flight of ideas, grandiose delusions (believes he is a famous film director), and marked distractibility. Insight is impaired. Which diagnostic pattern does this MSE cluster most strongly suggest?

answers.text: Paranoid schizophrenia — the grandiose delusions indicate a primary psychotic disorder.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. In paranoid schizophrenia, affect is typically flat or incongruent; mood elevation and flight of ideas are not characteristic features. Grandiose delusions can occur in both schizophrenia and mania, but the accompanying MSE picture (elevated mood, pressured speech, flight of ideas) points strongly away from schizophrenia.

answers.text: Manic episode (with psychotic features) — the combination of elevated mood, pressured speech, flight of ideas, and grandiosity is the classic MSE signature.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The full MSE cluster — elevated and expansive affect, pressured speech, flight of ideas, grandiose delusions, distractibility, and impaired insight — is the canonical presentation of a manic episode, often with psychotic features. ICD-11 requires the manic episode to be distinguished from secondary (organic) mania before diagnosing bipolar disorder.

answers.text: Major depressive episode with psychotic features — psychotic features can occur in depression.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Depressive psychosis would show low mood, psychomotor slowing, and mood-congruent psychotic features (nihilistic or guilt-laden delusions). Elevated mood and flight of ideas exclude a depressive episode.

answers.text: Delirium — the disorientation and behavioural change indicate an organic cause.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Delirium characteristically features disorientation, fluctuating consciousness, and visual hallucinations — none of which are present in this MSE. The sustained elevated mood, pressured speech, and flight of ideas are incompatible with delirium.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the MSE interpretation section. Identify the specific combination of mood, speech rate, thought-form, and thought-content findings that characterise manic episodes and distinguish them from primary psychosis.

Excellent MSE pattern recognition. Elevated mood + pressured speech + flight of ideas + grandiosity = manic episode signature. This MSE cluster should trigger systematic exclusion of organic mania (substance use, thyroid disease, CNS lesions).
